about.title: Desert Hot Springs Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Desert Hot Springs sits in Riverside County, where construction, hospitality, and agriculture jobs are common, and so are on-the-job injuries. Workers hurt on the clock often assume workers' compensation is their only option, but that's not always true. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on roads like Palm Drive or Hacienda Avenue contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may be possible alongside a workers' comp filing. Navigating both systems at once can be confusing, especially while recovering from an injury and dealing with missed paychecks. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured workers with an independent personal injury attorney who can help sort out which claims apply and what deadlines matter. We're not a law firm, and we don't charge for the connection. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: Why Injured Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Sort Out Which Claim Applies
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party can open the door to a separate injury claim. An attorney can help figure out if that applies to your situation.

items.title: Deadlines Matter and We Help You Move Fast
items.desc: Employer injury reports are generally due within 30 days, while third-party injury claims carry a two-year deadline in California. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and You Deserve Support
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or file a claim. Connecting with an attorney early can help protect your rights if you're worried about pushback at work.

items.question: I was hurt working near Dillon Road — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, you'll still file a workers' compensation claim with your employer since that's usually the exclusive remedy regardless of fault. But if a third party, like a subcontractor, driver, or equipment maker, contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate injury claim worth exploring. An independent attorney can help you understand which paths apply to your specific situation.

items.question: What if my employer in Desert Hot Springs tries to punish me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for employers to retaliate against workers who report an on-the-job injury or file a workers' comp claim. If you're facing pushback, documenting what happens and speaking with an attorney can help protect your rights moving forward.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we're not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
